clue.text: Stern assertion from stag to his mate?

definitions.meaning: the stern is the back of a ship

definitions.text: assertion from stag to his mate?
definitions.meaning: split as ..., this is a male deer telling a female deer what she is: a hind is a female red deer

explanation.surface: A wildlife-documentary question about what a stag might say firmly to his partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, 'be hind', for the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's stern is its rear, and the behind is the rear part of something.

clue.text: Author's cake dipped in tea? Au contraire

definitions.note: read as 'Author is', so the definition is the author himself

indicators.note: something dipped in a liquid ends up surrounded by it, so one piece goes inside another
French for 'on the contrary': the containment works the other way, the tea going into the cake rather than the cake into the tea

parts.note: a bun is a small round cake
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A picture of a famous writer dunking a cake in a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Au contraire' (on the contrary) flips the plain reading of 'dipped in': the tea goes into the cake. Cha is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: John Buchan was a Scottish novelist, best known for The Thirty-Nine Steps.

clue.text: Ground zero's hit, pinning western guns

indicators.note: pinning holds something fast in the middle, so the anagrammed letters hold the western letter within them
ground is the past participle of grind, so these letters are crushed and remade

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving the letters of zeros

explanation.surface: A wartime scene: artillery hitting ground zero while pinned down from the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' is the anagram signal, not the ground of 'ground zero'; it gives HOITZERS, and 'pinning' holds W inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Howitzers are short-barrelled artillery pieces firing shells on a high trajectory, a type of gun.

clue.text: Tiny baby consumed by gas

parts.note: neon is a noble gas
consumed food means ate it

explanation.surface: A worrying picture of a newborn overcome by gas fumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed by gas' reads as a passive, but it is two pieces side by side, with the gas first.
explanation.definitionFit: A neonate is a newborn infant, in its first weeks of life.

clue.text: Visit kitchen regularly and pick dessert

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth of kitchen

parts.note: the pick of something is its best part, the cream

explanation.surface: Pop into the kitchen often and choose a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'kitchen', giving ICE; 'Visit' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice cream is a frozen sweet served as a pudding at the end of a meal.

clue.text: Free speech semi-ostracises some men

indicators.note: free here means loosened or released, so the letters are let go into a new order
semi means half, so only the second half of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A political line: free speech partly shuts out certain people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi' keeps CISES, half of 'ostracises'; 'Free' shuffles it with SPEECH.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the pieces are often called men, so chess pieces are some of those men.

clue.text: Continue with cliffs just after cutting south

indicators.note: cutting a letter out of a word means removing it

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff, so scarry describes ground full of them
on can mean immediately after, as in 'on arrival'

explanation.surface: Directions for a walker: keep going alongside the cliffs, turning south soon after.
explanation.walkthrough: SCARRY ON with 'cutting' removing S for south leaves the answer; a scar is a crag.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on is to keep going, a phrasal-verb synonym for proceed or persist.

clue.text: Possibly wide on the right, not top or bottom

indicators.note: in a down clue, the top and bottom of a word are its first and last letters, both dropped here

parts.note: dextral means on or of the right-hand side

explanation.surface: A cricket or football commentary: maybe a wide player out on the right wing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach, which gives the batting side a run without being hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide is one kind of extra, a run in cricket not scored off the bat, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Steep promotion in naval affairs

indicators.note: in places the promotion inside the naval word

parts.note: the marine means a nation's shipping and naval matters, as in the mercantile marine
an ad promotes a product

explanation.surface: A sharp rise in rank within the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' is a verb meaning soak, not an adjective about the size of a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Food steeped in a seasoned liquid is marinated; a marinade is both the liquid and the soaking.

clue.text: Dodgy workman evasive about old bishop drinking whiskey

indicators.note: about means around, so the shy word goes around the rest

parts.note: coy means reluctant to give details, evasive

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so the old bishop letters hold the whiskey letter

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Whiskey is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for W

explanation.surface: A shifty tradesman avoiding questions about an elderly bishop who drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' puts W inside OB to make OWB, and 'about' has COY round that.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy, in British usage, is an unscrupulous or incompetent tradesman who does shoddy work.

clue.text: I hunt, following river around eastern French land after backtracking

indicators.note: around means the two outer letters enclose what follows

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: backtracking means going back over a route, so these letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: terre is the French word for land

explanation.surface: A hunter's account of tracking along a river and doubling back across French territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backtracking' turns E + TERRE into ERRETE, which F and R go 'around'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferreter is one who hunts with ferrets, so 'I hunt' is a self-description by such a person.

clue.text: For whom workers may make meals

definitions.text: For whom workers may make meals

parts.words: For whom workers may make meals
parts.note: workers here are worker ants, which become food for those that feed on them, rather than cooks preparing food

explanation.surface: Seems to describe diners whose meals are cooked by staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' is a crossword staple for ants, and they are the meal, not the cooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Anteaters are mammals that feed on ants and termites with long sticky tongues.

clue.text: Was part of internet node corrupted when deleting a name

indicators.note: corrupted data is scrambled, so these letters are rearranged
deleting signals that a letter is taken out of the scrambled pool

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A computing mishap: a network node corrupted when a name was deleted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupted' shuffles INTERNET NODE, and 'when deleting' takes one N out of the pool first.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter into something, such as an agreement, is to become a party to it, to take part.

clue.text: Long time before November

parts.note: a year is a period of time
November is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for N

explanation.surface: A long stretch of time before the month of November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is a verb meaning to desire, not an adjective about time.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn for it; both verbs mean to want something intensely.

clue.text: Raced topless around Sinai Desert, otherwise walked

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is taken off

parts.note: sped means raced

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: A runner dashing shirtless across the Sinai, or else just strolling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is only a link here; 'otherwise' is the anagram signal and 'topless' drops the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrianise can be intransitive, meaning to go about on foot, so pedestrianised is a rare word for walked.

clue.text: Croft girl slicing fish — think something's odd?

indicators.note: slicing cuts into something, so the girl's name goes inside the fish

parts.note: a smelt is a small silvery fish
Lara Croft is the heroine of the Tomb Raider video games

explanation.surface: Lara Croft cutting up a fish, and something seeming not quite right.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell a rat is an idiom for suspecting that something is wrong or underhand.

clue.text: Impressive understanding has moved husband

indicators.note: the husband's letter is shifted to a new place within the word

parts.note: empathic means understanding others' feelings

explanation.surface: A sympathetic, understanding person has relocated her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has moved' shifts the H of EMPATHIC two places earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphatic means forceful and striking, which is what something impressive is.

clue.text: Was unaware of short girl having grown

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Miss is the title for a girl or unmarried woman
an asset that has appreciated has grown in value

explanation.surface: Someone failing to notice that a little girl has grown up.
explanation.definitionFit: To misappreciate is to fail to grasp the true worth or nature of something, to be unaware of it.

clue.text: Composer by trade, you say?

indicators.note: you say means the letters follow how the words are spoken, not spelt

parts.note: per means by, as in 'per post'; to sell is to trade

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone is a composer by profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by trade' looks like a phrase about a job, but it is PER + SELL, spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Purcell was a leading English Baroque composer, writer of Dido and Aeneas.

clue.text: Wild in the past, entertaining rising French director

indicators.note: entertaining guests means taking them in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: ago means in the past

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so the name is reversed

parts.note: Jacques Tati was a French film director, maker of Monsieur Hulot's Holiday

explanation.surface: A rowdy past spent hosting a French film-maker on the way up.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitato is a musical direction meaning to play in an agitated, restless way.

clue.text: Several monarchs embracing single European change

indicators.note: embracing means holding in the arms, so the monarchs go around the single

parts.note: K, R and R are three abbreviations for a king: K, R for rex, and R for roi
single means one

explanation.surface: Kings and queens grasping one piece of European small change.
explanation.definitionFit: The krone (plural kroner) is the currency of Denmark and Norway, so kroner are European money.

clue.text: Hesitate? Barber doesn't begin

indicators.note: doesn't begin means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a barber is someone who shaves customers, a shaver

explanation.surface: A barber's hesitation before the first cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To haver, chiefly Scottish and northern English, is to dither or vacillate.

clue.text: Somebody regularly heard weasel

parts.note: a somebody is an important person, a VIP

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Someone often heard to sound like a sneaky little animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' is not a homophone here; 'regularly' takes its even letters, ER. 'Weasel' is a person, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A viper and a weasel are both used for a treacherous, untrustworthy person.

clue.text: Maybe Macduff's princess yet to meet her mother-in-law

definitions.note: read as 'Maybe Macduff is'; Macduff is a Scottish whisky distillery

parts.note: Di is Diana, Princess of Wales
still means yet, as in 'still to come'
Diana's mother-in-law was Queen Elizabeth II, ER (Elizabeth Regina)

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean scene: Macduff's princess still to meet her husband's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Macduff suggests Macbeth, but it is a distillery town on the Moray coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Macduff is the name of a Scotch whisky distillery, and a distillery is a distiller, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Cheap deposit backed with very little money

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to put something down is to deposit it
a penny is a very small sum

explanation.surface: A small deposit paid with hardly any cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuppenny, from twopenny, means worth very little: cheap or trifling.

clue.text: Sister's pal picked up unbridled sarcasm

definitions.note: read as 'Sister is'; a Sister is a senior nurse

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the letters follow how the word sounds

parts.note: a mate is a pal

indicators.note: unbridled means with the restraints at each end taken off, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: irony is mocking language close to sarcasm

explanation.surface: A nun's friend catching a cutting remark.
explanation.walkthrough: MATRON is said 'MAY-tron', so its MAT sounds like MATE.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a matron was the senior nurse in charge, and nurses are called Sister.

clue.text: Bells of Ireland back in demand

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters inside the demand word

parts.note: to call on someone is to demand something of them

indicators.note: back means the letters are turned round

parts.note: Ir is an abbreviation for Ireland or Irish

explanation.surface: Irish bells coming back into demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bells of Ireland' is a garden plant, but 'Bells' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A carillon is a set of tuned bells played from a keyboard.

clue.text: Tamper with bones

definitions.meaning: to falsify or interfere with it
bones, short for sawbones, is slang for a ..., a surgeon

explanation.surface: Interfering with a skeleton.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctoring evidence is tampering with it; sawbones is old slang for a physician.
